items.title: Ed Soph interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 9, 2024
items.q: Yeah there was an early jazz writer, Whitney Balliett, I think he said, “Jazz is the sound of surprise.”

ctx.x: imaginations. Because if you don’t use your imagination that’s when you get bored. And I mean you lived for those, you had 22 hours off and two hours on, you know? And you’d ride that damn stinking bus for hours just in anticipation of getting on the bandstand and going after it. And every night was a new experience. Sometimes good, sometimes not so good. But at any rate it was there. And that’s what — Woody loved that. There were times when I would deliberately leave out a big fill that I usually played and the…
Yeah there was an early jazz writer, Whitney Balliett, I think he said, “Jazz is the sound of surprise.”
Yeah, exactly, yeah. So Woody was fine with that sort of thing.
